sources.title: Meta-analysis of the effects of dietary inclusion of brewers grains on lactating dairy cows
sources.locator: PubMed abstract: 12 peer-reviewed articles; n=472 dairy cows; effects and dose-response up to 20% BG
sources.finding: Across 12 articles and 472 cows, BG modestly reduced DMI and increased feed efficiency; milk fat/protein concentrations were not affected.
sources.scope: Lactating dairy cows; pooled studies 1983-2021; not Aass-specific or Norwegian

sources.title: Wet brewers grains for lactating dairy cows during hot, humid weather
sources.locator: PubMed abstract: 20 lactating Jersey cows; 0/15/30% wet brewers grains plus yeast arm
sources.finding: DMI and milk yield did not differ across control and wet-grain treatments; milk protein percentage was lower with wet brewers grains.
sources.scope: 20 Jersey cows; hot humid US climate; wet BSG; diet-specific result

sources.title: Use of dried brewers' grains instead of soybean meal to feed lactating cows
sources.locator: Abstract/Methods/Results: 5 Holstein cows; 5x5 Latin square; 0/25/50/75/100% dried BG replacing soybean meal; 100% DMI 4.4 kg/d lower
sources.finding: The small dried-BG replacement study found dose-related intake/energy trade-offs and a 4.4 kg/d lower DMI at 100% replacement; it does not establish wet Aass-mask soy substitution.
sources.scope: Five lactating Holstein cows in Brazil; dried BSG; isonitrogenous 50:50 forage:concentrate diet
sources.comparison_note: Distinct from existing forcase S4: South African Journal of Animal Science study used 4 rumen-cannulated Jersey oxen, 4x4 Latin square, and 0/33/66/100% DBG; this source used 5 lactating Holstein cows, 5x5 Latin square, and 0/25/50/75/100% DBG.

sources.title: The variability of physico-chemical properties of brewery spent grain from 8 different breweries
sources.locator: Methods and Table 1: eight breweries; convective drying max 70 C; moisture 2.178-4.353%; protein 22.217-30.236%
sources.finding: Between-brewery variation is measured in dried samples; these percentages are not a wet Aass specification.
sources.scope: Eight European breweries; dried analytical samples; composition study, not Aass and not feeding trial
